A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DisPOSE research and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. The supplied material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original DisPOSE evaluations on Panoptic, MM-OR Pose, Shelf, and Campus, plus ablations, robustness tests, and computational measurements.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical evaluations and reports revised Panoptic pose-estimation and ablation results.

M1.justification: Sections 3 and Appendix A retain the same projected diffusion, Sinkhorn normalization, hypergraph decoder, triangulation, losses, and sampling algorithm. The revised results are not accompanied by a documented method change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four datasets and retain the same camera-generalization scenarios, occluded surgical scenes, unusual-pose examples, and root-perturbation conditions.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding experiments. In particular, Table 6 retains V2V-Net and MVGFormer, while Tables 12–13 retain MvPose and COMPOSE; revised scores do not introduce new baselines.

E3.justification: Table 11 changes the stated pose-error metric heading from MDE to MPJPE, a limited reporting correction; a different computation is not established. Dataset splits, training budgets, camera configurations, evaluation thresholds, and root-noise settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Existing decoder, camera-count, supervision-source, and root-error analyses receive revised evidence in Tables 6, 10, 11, and 14. The root-error analysis now reports substantially smaller perturbation penalties. No new ablation conditions or qualitative cases are introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same ten-seed mean and standard-error procedure for Table 5, the same rationale for omitting uncertainty elsewhere, and the same runtime uncertainty entries in Table 17.

E6.justification: Central Panoptic pose results change substantially under the same reported settings: Table 1 AP25 rises from 68.59 to 82.68 and MPJPE falls from 21.20 to 18.91 mm. Tables 4, 6, 10, 11, and 14 also change, including both decoder baselines in Table 6. Table 10's seven-view pose mAP decreases from 95.65 to 94.50, producing a decline from six to seven views in v3. Root-localization results, other datasets, and computational measurements remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The tensor and marginal definitions, Sinkhorn formulation, diffusion equations, triangulation equations, and loss formulations are retained. No theorem, proof, formal assumption, or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The introduction strengthens its quantitative contribution claims: the Panoptic AP25 advantage changes from 19% to 25 percentage points, and the highlighted unseen-camera mAP changes from 75% to 89% against 59%. The methodological, benchmark, and data-efficiency contributions retain their scope.

C2.justification: Appendix D.3 replaces the harder-detections explanation for ground-truth-root results with an interpretation of effective insensitivity to residual Stage-I errors, and emphasizes occasionally surpassing ground-truth supervision at coarse thresholds. Section 4.2 newly calls AP150 the largest cross-dataset drop, although Tables 1–2 show a larger AP50 drop. The limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 adds a project-site/code access pointer to the abstract. Implementation specifications, hardware, hyperparameters, and data-processing details are unchanged. Both versions retain the future-tense code-release statement and the incomplete Appendix A.3 placeholder.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning remain unchanged. V3 adds an unfinished note requesting a higher-order synchronization reference, but supplies no additional citation or substantive comparison.

P1.justification: Changes comprise localized results-discussion rewrites, wording and punctuation corrections, and a conference publication notice replacing the preprint notice. The section organization remains intact. Appendix C gains a visible unfinished author TODO.

P2.justification: The same 13 figures and 18 tables are retained without substantial redesign. Changes include local text/table reflow, Table 6's placement within page 8, Table 11's corrected metric heading, and a small Figure 11 caption correction.

improvement.justification: The access pointer and metric-label correction are useful, but v3 introduces substantive text–table inconsistencies. V1's Table 10 pose mAP rises to its seven-view peak; v3 peaks at 96.45% with six views and falls to 94.50% with seven, while Appendix D.1 still claims monotonic improvement and a seven-view peak. Section 4.2 also introduces the incorrect largest-drop interpretation, and Appendix C gains an unfinished TODO. These limited consistency and presentation regressions outweigh the documentation fixes; higher reported scores alone do not establish improved paper quality.
